verifiedFindings: The Andalusian tourism authority identifies Sierra Morena as a Starlight Reserve and destination spanning the Sierra Norte de Sevilla natural park.

The Constantina municipality documents a registered astronomy event at Castillo de Constantina; the provincial heritage register supplies the castle name and coordinates, but the dated event does not establish routine night access.

The Almadén de la Plata municipality identifies its astronomical observatory at Mirador de La Traviesa, about five kilometres outside the town; the mapped observatory feature supplies the corrected coordinate.
The observatory operator currently directs astronomy activities to El Castillo de las Guardas, so the Almadén site cannot be presented as a currently operating independent stop.

requiredChanges.reason: Obtain current operator or municipal confirmation of an actual bookable programme before clearing the factual gate; until then the guide must remain confirmation-first and the destination inactive.

verifiedFindings: The Cáceres provincial biosphere-reserve tourism authority explicitly identifies both Castillo de Monfragüe and Salto del Gitano as places for astronomical observation.
The authority's castle page describes designated parking followed by an approximately 20-minute walk and stairs; its route link locates the castle at 39.8281476, -6.0514947.
The authority's Salto del Gitano page describes access by car, motorcycle, bicycle or a signed walk from Villarreal de San Carlos; its route link locates the viewpoint at 39.8285483, -6.0578331.
The national-park visitor rules require use of designated viewpoint parking, prohibit camping and limit caravan or motorhome parking between 22:00 and 06:00 to no more than two consecutive hours.

The national-park itinerary page confirms Castillo de Monfragüe as a signed self-guided route and Salto del Gitano as a principal park viewpoint; current notices still take precedence over the prepared itinerary.

The Ávila provincial tourism authority identifies Navarredonda de Gredos and Hoyos del Espino as members of its purpose-built stellar-viewpoint network, whose facilities include a stable observing platform, parking, fencing, accessibility features and signed access.

The Navarredonda municipality documents a 23:00 astronomy event at Mirador Estelar de Navarredonda de Gredos, confirming night use of the named facility; the mapped viewpoint supplies the corrected coordinate 40.36303, -5.12396.

The Hoyos del Espino municipality documents a 22:30 astronomy event at Mirador Estelar Mesegosillo (Las Cocinillas), confirming night use of the named facility; the mapped viewpoint supplies the corrected coordinate 40.35239, -5.16424.
The Ávila Provincial Council states that the Sierra de Gredos Regional Park's Starlight Reserve certification was renewed in January 2025 for another four years.
The official sources support the named astronomy facilities but do not grant camping or override current local signs, temporary restrictions or mountain-weather decisions.
Galáctica's official visitor page documents bookable nighttime observations with professional telescopes, onsite parking, cold-weather advice and a weather-dependent cancellation process.
Galáctica's current activity calendar lists dated evening astronomy sessions, so the centre is represented as a booking-only programme venue rather than an independently accessible night site.
The official directions link identifies Galáctica at 39.9991162, -1.0407695, replacing the generic Arcos de las Salinas map point.
CEFCA locates the Observatorio Astrofísico de Javalambre at 40.0412972, -1.0164167 and 1,957 metres, while warning that its tracks require careful access planning and recommending a 4x4 vehicle.

The OAJ and Galáctica visitor pages route public OAJ visits through Galáctica and explicitly describe the OAJ visit as outreach rather than direct observing; it is therefore not presented as an independent night-observing stop.
Neither a Galáctica booking nor the regional Starlight context grants camping, after-hours access or permission to approach the research observatory outside the booked visitor arrangement.

The official Vall de Boí destination page identifies the national park and surrounding valley as a Starlight destination and explicitly names astronomical viewpoints at Boí Taüll and Sant Quirc de Durro.

The Boí Taüll Starlight viewpoint is located on the accessible walkway from car park P2, includes a planisphere for independent night-sky interpretation and hosts observing sessions on selected dates; the official station map confirms the parking, accessible route and Starlight facility layout.

The mapped P2 parking arrival area is 42.4793803, 0.8666296. It is used as the navigable coordinate because the official destination describes the viewpoint as reached from that car park rather than publishing a separate point coordinate.

The official Sant Quirc viewpoint page embeds the coordinate 42.4951864, 0.8111783 and states that independent visitors must walk about 20 minutes from the parking area at Durro's entrance; taxi access may be arranged.

The national-park authority states that private vehicles must remain at authorized entrance parking and that access inside the park continues on foot or by 4x4 taxi. Estany de Sant Maurici therefore cannot be presented as an independent drive-up observing stop.

Boí replaces Espot as the guide base because both verified astronomical viewpoints are in Vall de Boí; current signs, station operations, mountain weather and the published return route still determine whether either night visit proceeds.

The Vercors park authority and DarkSky International confirm that the southern three-quarters of the park form a 1,600-square-kilometre International Dark Sky Reserve designated in 2023, with a 245-square-kilometre core zone.
The Trièves tourism office identifies the public astronomy observatory at Résidence Les Dolomites, publishes the exact coordinate 44.90013, 5.554026 and gives precise visitor entrance directions.

The observatory's current listing publishes telescope-observing sessions for July, August and December 2026 and February, July and August 2027; the site is therefore represented as programme-only, not as independently open at night.

The official Gresse-en-Vercors visitor map marks both the astronomy observatory and nearby visitor parking, corroborating the named visitor setting without turning the coordinate into permission for after-hours access or camping.

Vercors Drôme Tourisme documents the 2026 Nuit des étoiles at Moulins de la Mure, including the exact coordinate 44.914771, 5.379652, evening sky interpretation and a weather fallback. The dated event does not establish routine access, so the venue is usable only when a new programme is published.

The generic Col de la Machine and Vassieux plateau pins lacked source support as specific astronomy visitor sites and are replaced by these two documented programme venues; Gresse-en-Vercors becomes the return base for the primary observatory plan.

The Sternenpark authority explicitly identifies Tauchplatz Dixi and Taferlklaussee among six designated Sternderl-schau’n visitor places and directs visitors to named public or hiking car parks, established paths and leave-no-trace conduct.
The Attersee-Attergau tourism authority confirms the Sternenpark's International Dark Sky recognition since 2021 and repeats both named observing places in its visitor guidance.

The official Dixi visitor listing identifies the site at B152 kilometre 10.6 in Weyregg, lists year-round operation, 20 parking spaces and a WC; the official tourism PDF publishes a coordinate within about 100 metres of the independent dive-coordinate reference 47.864608, 13.563412.

The official Taferlklaussee route describes the small car park directly at the lake, a larger nearby parking option and an elevation range of 772 to 786 metres; the published event meeting point locates the Taferlklausstube parking area at 47.843838, 13.626818.

The Sternenpark visitor rules require designated parking and marked paths and prohibit wild camping and fires. Both sites therefore remain limited-access shared visitor places rather than unrestricted night or camping locations.
Weyregg replaces Unterach as the return base because it is the municipality of the primary Dixi site and the official destination page publishes the town coordinate 47.90, 13.57.
